### Using the prefix option

If your project has class names that conflict with Tailwind CSS utilities, you can prefix all Tailwind-generated classes and CSS variables using the `prefix` option:

<CodeExampleStack>

```css
/* [!code filename:app.css] */
/* [!code word:important] */
@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);
```

```css
/* [!code filename:Compiled CSS] */
/* [!code word:tw\:] */
@layer theme {
  :root {
    --tw-color-red-500: oklch(0.637 0.237 25.331);
  }
}

@layer utilities {
  .tw\:text-red-500 {
    color: var(--tw-color-red-500);
  }
}
```

</CodeExampleStack>
405:To completely override an entire namespace in the default theme, set the entire namespace to `initial` using the special asterisk syntax:
413:  --color-*: initial;
428:To completely disable the default theme and use only custom values, set the global theme variable namespace to `initial`:
436:  --*: initial;
516:This happens because `var(--font-sans)` is resolved where `--font-sans` is defined _(on `#parent`)_, and `--font-inter` has no value there since it's not defined until deeper in the tree _(on `#child`)_.
540:  --*: initial;

content.text:
No, it isn't safe to leave your variables unprefixed, but v4 gives you a built-in fix: the `prefix()` option.

- **Use `prefix()`:** `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` prefixes both classes and CSS variables. For example, the output has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500`. See `src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Using the prefix option".
- **Keep configuring the theme without the prefix:** `src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx` says to define theme variables as if you aren't using a prefix. Tailwind adds it on output.
- **Unused variables:** by default only used CSS variables are generated. So you already don't ship the whole default `--color-*` set unless you use `@theme static`. See `src/docs/theme.mdx`, the `static` option.
- **Keeping `rounded-lg` and dropping the rest:** you don't need to reset the defaults. Keep `--radius-*` and set `--color-*: initial;` for the namespaces you replace (`theme.mdx`, "Customizing your theme").

I didn't find a doc that says whether the prefix also covers variables you define yourself in `@theme`. Check that on a compiled build.

- **Use `prefix()`:** `@import "tailwindcss" prefix(tw);` prefixes both classes and CSS variables. For example, the output has `--tw-color-red-500` and `.tw\:text-red-500`. See `src/docs/styling-with-utility-classes.mdx`, "Using the prefix option".
- **Keep configuring the theme without the prefix:** `src/docs/upgrade-guide.mdx` says to define theme variables as if you aren't using a prefix. Tailwind adds it on output.
- **Unused variables:** by default only used CSS variables are generated. So you already don't ship the whole default `--color-*` set unless you use `@theme static`. See `src/docs/theme.mdx`, the `static` option.
- **Keeping `rounded-lg` and dropping the rest:** you don't need to reset the defaults. Keep `--radius-*` and set `--color-*: initial;` for the namespaces you replace (`theme.mdx`, "Customizing your theme").

I didn't find a doc that says whether the prefix also covers variables you define yourself in `@theme`. Check that on a compiled build.
